_comment: Provenance for the compiled contract blueprints served by this backend: the CIP-113 core, the upstream rwa-token module, and four first-party modules.
The core and rwa-token Aiken source lives upstream; the four first-party module source trees live in this repository under src/modules/.
Repository and commit identify the original source revision. For older first-party commits, the source path was src/substandards/<name>/.
ContractBlueprintPinTest verifies these artifact hashes; docs/CONTRACTS.md explains reproduction and the metadata-only module rename.

blueprints.name: cip113-core
blueprints.note: Upstream's committed plutus.json, byte for byte. It reproduces from source with aiken v1.1.23+8949565: all 34 validator entries and the complete artifact are identical. The SDK pins and operates this exact artifact.

blueprints.name: rwa-token
blueprints.note: NOT upstream's committed plutus.json. Upstream's is STALE: at this commit it does not reproduce from its own source -- global_state.global_state_spend_validator is committed as 57e2c6d5ca432b24871d113a1f0f4664ca4ea574d8ce892537356f49 (4901 bytes) where the source compiles to e720eb536b26eb8c639e96a17de4404ab4dbf18224ae9cc2242e13a9 (4698 bytes). plutus.json and validators/global_state.ak were last touched by the SAME commit, so the blueprint was committed without being regenerated after a final source edit. We ship the REBUILD, because the script that goes on chain must be the source that gets audited. Reproduce it by rebuilding upstream at this commit -- see docs/CONTRACTS.md. upstream_committed_sha256 records the stale bytes so it stays possible to tell whether upstream has since regenerated.

blueprints.name: dummy
blueprints.note: In-repo module: at the pinned commit the source and committed artifact are in src/substandards/dummy/; this working tree now places them in src/modules/dummy/. The served blueprint is byte-for-byte identical to the artifact at that commit. Rebuild there with the pinned compiler.

blueprints.name: freeze-and-seize
blueprints.note: At the pinned commit, source and the committed blueprint are in src/substandards/freeze-and-seize/. For this terminology rename, the manifest description was changed from the former term to module and rebuilt with the pinned compiler; the only blueprint difference is preamble.description. All validator entries and script hashes are byte-for-byte identical. To reproduce the served bytes, check out that commit, change the description in src/substandards/freeze-and-seize/aiken.toml to the current wording, and run aiken build with the pinned compiler. upstream_committed_sha256 records the original committed artifact.
